title: Proxmox VE
description: Proxmox VE cluster: nodes, storage and guests, from the metrics Proxmox pushes itself (service proxmox-ve). Provisioned from git (kube-cluster/external/proxmox).

links.title: Ceph cluster
links.tooltip: Health and capacity of the Ceph cluster behind the shared storages

panels.title: Nodes reporting
panels.description: Nodes whose metrics arrived in the last minutes. Fewer than the cluster has: a node is down, or its metric server push or the OTel gateway is broken.

panels.title: Nodes missing
panels.description: Nodes seen in the last 24h that report nothing now. Anything above 0 is bad: the node is down, or Proxmox stopped pushing. A node removed on purpose shows for 24h.

panels.title: Guests running
panels.description: Guests with an uptime above 0. Currently all guests are QEMU VMs (no containers).

panels.title: Guests stopped
panels.description: Guests that are defined but not running (uptime 0). Expected for a few; a guest that should run and is listed here needs a look.

panels.title: Inactive storages
panels.description: Storage definitions a node reports as not active (unmounted, Ceph unreachable). Anything above 0 is bad: guests on it cannot start.

panels.title: Fullest storage
panels.description: The storage with the highest used share, cluster-wide. Above 85% is bad; see the Storage row for the trend.

panels.title: Cluster CPU
panels.description: Used share of all CPU threads of the selected nodes. Sustained above 80% leaves no headroom for a node failover.

panels.title: Cluster memory
panels.description: Used share of all node memory, including ZFS ARC (which gives memory back under pressure). Above 90% means a node failover cannot fit.

panels.title: Storage used
panels.description: Used share per storage. Shared storages (Ceph) are counted once; local ones per node. Above 85% is bad, above 95% critical.

targets.expr: proxmox_storage_used{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} / proxmox_storage_total{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} and on (node, storage) (proxmox_storage_shared{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} == 0)

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Used share of each node's CPU threads. Sustained above 80% is bad.

panels.title: CPU I/O wait
panels.description: Share of time CPUs wait for disk or network storage. Above a few percent for minutes means slow Ceph or local disks.

panels.title: Load per core (5 min)
panels.description: 5 minute load average divided by the thread count. Sustained above 1 means runnable tasks queue for a CPU.

panels.title: Memory available
panels.description: Share of memory the kernel can hand out without swapping (MemAvailable, ZFS ARC excluded). Below 10% is bad; Proxmox's own 'used' counts the ARC as used.

panels.title: Memory used and total
panels.description: Used (including ZFS ARC) against the installed memory. Used close to total is bad unless ARC accounts for it (next panel).

panels.title: ZFS ARC
panels.description: ZFS cache size against its maximum. It is counted in memory used and shrinks under pressure; it is not a leak.

panels.title: Root filesystem used
panels.description: Used share of each node's root filesystem. Above 85% is bad: logs and the Proxmox database live there.

panels.title: Swap used
panels.description: Swap in use. The nodes have no swap configured, so this stays 0; any value means swap was added and memory is tight.

panels.title: Network receive
panels.description: Receive rate per physical NIC (en*/eth*; bridges, taps and loopback would count the same bytes twice). A NIC far from its neighbours or stuck at 0 is suspect.

panels.title: Network transmit
panels.description: Transmit rate per physical NIC (en*/eth*). Compare with receive: Ceph traffic is symmetric between nodes.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the node booted. A node far below its neighbours rebooted recently (kernel update or crash).

panels.title: Shared storage
panels.description: Shared storages are listed once; Proxmox reports them from every node. Time to full is the 7 day linear trend of free space; empty when free space is not falling.

targets.expr: (max by (storage) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster"}) / -deriv(max by (storage) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster"})[7d:1h]) and deriv(max by (storage) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster"})[7d:1h]) < 0) and on (storage) (max by (storage) (proxmox_storage_shared{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster"}) == 1)

panels.title: Local storage
panels.description: Per-node storages (root disk, ZFS pools). A local storage near full stops guests on that node.

targets.expr: proxmox_storage_used{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} / proxmox_storage_total{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} and on (node, storage) (proxmox_storage_shared{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} == 0)

(max by (storage, node) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"}) / -deriv(max by (storage, node) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"})[7d:1h]) and deriv(max by (storage, node) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"})[7d:1h]) < 0) and on (node, storage) (proxmox_storage_shared{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} == 0)

panels.title: Time to full
panels.description: Seconds until free space reaches 0 at the 7 day linear trend (the retired ceph-storage-fill rules used the same). Only storages whose free space is falling are listed. Under 14 days is bad, under 3 days critical. Pools grow in steps, so read it as a hint, not a forecast.

targets.expr: (max by (storage) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster"}) / -deriv(max by (storage) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster"})[7d:1h]) and deriv(max by (storage) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster"})[7d:1h]) < 0) and on (storage) (max by (storage) (proxmox_storage_shared{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster"}) == 1)

(max by (storage, node) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"}) / -deriv(max by (storage, node) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"})[7d:1h]) and deriv(max by (storage, node) (proxmox_storage_avail{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"})[7d:1h]) < 0) and on (node, storage) (proxmox_storage_shared{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} == 0)

panels.title: Shared storage used
panels.description: Used share per shared storage over time. A steady climb is growth; a step is a large copy or a restore.

panels.title: Local storage used
panels.description: Used share per node-local storage over time.

targets.expr: proxmox_storage_used{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} / proxmox_storage_total{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} and on (node, storage) (proxmox_storage_shared{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} == 0)

panels.title: Guests
panels.description: Every guest of the selected nodes (all QEMU VMs today). Memory above 100% means the guest uses more than its allotment (balloon or overhead). Disk usage is not reported for VMs, so only the size is shown.

targets.expr: proxmox_vm_mem{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node", name=~"$guest", type=~"$type"} / proxmox_vm_maxmem{"proxmox.cluster"=~"$cluster", node=~"$node", name=~"$guest", type=~"$type"}

panels.title: Top $topk guests by CPU
panels.description: Used share of the guest's own vCPUs; a guest pinned near 100% is starved of CPU. Stopped guests report 0 and drop out of the top list.

panels.title: Top $topk guests by memory
panels.description: Memory in use per guest. A guest at its allotment (maxmem) has nothing left for page cache. Stopped guests report 0 and drop out of the top list.

panels.title: Top $topk guests by disk read
panels.description: Read rate of all virtual disks. Stopped guests report 0 and drop out of the top list.

panels.title: Top $topk guests by disk write
panels.description: Write rate of all virtual disks. A guest writing far above its usual rate fills Ceph. Stopped guests report 0 and drop out of the top list.

panels.title: Top $topk guests by network in
panels.description: Receive rate of all virtual NICs. Stopped guests report 0 and drop out of the top list.

panels.title: Top $topk guests by network out
panels.description: Transmit rate of all virtual NICs. Stopped guests report 0 and drop out of the top list.

panels.title: Top $topk guests by CPU pressure
panels.description: Share of time at least one task of the guest waited for CPU (PSI 'some'). Sustained above 10% is bad: the guest or its node is CPU-starved. Stopped guests report 0 and drop out of the top list.

panels.title: Top $topk guests by I/O pressure
panels.description: Share of time at least one task of the guest waited for disk I/O (PSI 'some'). Sustained above 10% is bad: slow storage under the guest. Stopped guests report 0 and drop out of the top list.
